issue.title: Sandbox plexmediaserver with a systemd hardening drop-in on athena
issue.description:
Sandbox plexmediaserver on athena with a systemd drop-in so a future Plex RCE cannot read Bryan's home or persist outside Plex's data dir:

`ProtectHome=yes` (would have hidden the plaintext sudo password and API keys the 2026-10-17 attacker could read), `ProtectSystem=strict` + `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/plexmediaserver /mnt/hercules/plex`, `PrivateTmp=yes`, `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `NoExecPaths=/tmp /var/tmp /dev/shm`, `RestrictSUIDSGID=yes`, `ProtectKernelModules=yes`, `ProtectKernelTunables=yes`, `LockPersonality=yes`, and `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_NETLINK`. Must be validated against hardware transcoding (`/dev/dri`, render/video groups), DLNA, library scans of /mnt/hercules, and Plex's own updater/codec downloads; check `systemd-analyze security plexmediaserver` before/after.

Evidence: research:202610/athena_plex_compromise_incident_report.md ("Preventing a repeat" #3).

task_type_fields.proposal: systemd hardening drop-in for plexmediaserver (ProtectHome, ProtectSystem=strict, PrivateTmp, NoExecPaths, ...)
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Needs testing against hardware transcoding and library scans, which the approved incident plan did not scope.

issue.creation_reason: The Plex RCE could read every world-readable file in Bryan's home, including his sudo password; ProtectHome and related systemd options would have contained it.

payload.description: Same athena hardening pass: 8t sandboxes the Plex service; 8u removes a root supervisor control channel any service account could reach
